claim: Language-model agents can be helpful explainers of already-localized transformer circuits by recovering individual components’ functional roles and the computation implemented by the circuit as a whole. Helpfulness is established if at least one agent correctly classifies more than 50% of circuit components, achieves mean role-description quality above 0.50 on a 0–1 scale where 0, 0.5, and 1 represent incorrect, partially correct, and correct descriptions, and correctly identifies the overall task for more than 50% of circuits. Because the circuit is supplied in advance, the claim concerns explanation after localization rather than circuit discovery.

experiments: Build the controlled circuit-explanation benchmark. Start from the 84 RASP-derived semi-synthetic transformer models in InterpBench, excluding the two IOI tasks to reduce reliance on memorized circuit explanations, and trace each localized trained component through InterpBench’s high-level/low-level correspondence map to the RASP variable it implements. Manually annotate every component with a task-specific note and one of five tags—INDICATOR, AGGREGATOR, ROUTER, MAPPER, or COMBINER—and give each task its RASP program, ground-truth task description, and five input-output examples sampled from the task distribution and produced by executing the program. The resulting AGENTICINTERPBENCH contains 84 circuits and 163 components: 120 MLPs and 43 attention components, with 72 MAPPER, 32 AGGREGATOR, 33 COMBINER, 11 ROUTER, and 15 INDICATOR annotations; circuits contain 1.94 components on average, with a range of 1–10.

Fix the agent workflow and execution budget used for every benchmark run. For each supplied localized component, run HYVE’s observation, hypothesis-generation, and causal-validation loop, withholding the five-class taxonomy until the later classification stage; after processing all components, assign tags and role notes and infer the circuit’s task from the validated component hypotheses and input-output examples. Observation and validation code may use provided TransformerLens helper libraries or custom Python; failed code receives its error message and may be revised for up to five execution attempts per stage. Permit at most three hypothesis-validation iterations per component, retain the latest hypothesis as tentative if none is supported, and measure exact tag accuracy, role-description quality rescaled from judge scores of 0, 1, and 2 to 0, 0.5, and 1, binary task-description accuracy, and the fraction of execute_python calls that run without error.

Validate the LLM-scored explanation metrics against blinded human ratings. Have two human judges independently score anonymized and randomized HYVE outputs using the same role-description and task-description rubrics, and use the lower of their two scores as the human label, matching the lower-score aggregation used for GPT-5.4 and Gemini-3.1-Pro as LLM judges. On the cross-backbone subset of 10 tasks and 17 components, comprising 68 component-level and 40 task-level model-output instances, human-human agreement is κ=0.83 for role-description quality and κ=0.96 for task accuracy; agreement between the lower human score and lower LLM-judge score is κ=0.76 and κ=0.80, respectively. On the larger GPT-5.4/Claude-Sonnet-4.6 annotation set, comprising 110 component-level and 62 task-level instances, human-human agreement is κ=0.802 for role descriptions and κ=0.963 for task accuracy, while lower-human versus lower-LLM agreement is κ=0.753 and κ=0.864. Validation-plan soundness is less reliable: human-human κ is 0.37 on the cross-backbone subset and 0.460 on the larger subset, so the authors retain it as a process diagnostic rather than an official benchmark metric.

Test whether LM agents can explain supplied localized circuits. Run the full HYVE workflow over all 84 AGENTICINTERPBENCH circuits and 163 components with GPT-5.4, Claude-Sonnet-4.6, Gemini-3.1-Pro, and Qwen-3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct. GPT-5.4 obtains tag accuracy 0.74, role-description quality 0.46, task accuracy 0.63, and code-execution success 0.52; Claude-Sonnet-4.6 obtains 0.79, 0.58, 0.75, and 0.93; Gemini-3.1-Pro obtains 0.76, 0.59, 0.83, and 0.80; and Qwen-3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct obtains 0.67, 0.25, 0.25, and 0.62. Claude-Sonnet-4.6 has the highest component-tag accuracy, Gemini-3.1-Pro has the highest judged role-description and task accuracy, and no backbone is best on every metric.

Check that the reported backbone ordering is not produced by judge self-preference or a single stochastic run. Score role descriptions and task descriptions separately with GPT-5.4 and Gemini-3.1-Pro rather than only using their lower-score aggregate, and repeat runs on a fixed benchmark subset. Both judges give the same backbone ranking for task accuracy; for role-description quality, both place GPT-5.4 third and Qwen fourth, while Claude-Sonnet-4.6 and Gemini-3.1-Pro exchange the top two positions with only a small score difference. The authors report no consistent advantage for a judge’s own model family, and the repeated runs preserve the backbone-level trends.
